events.title: Perihelion at 0.256 AU (pre-discovery)
events.description: 'Oumuamua made its closest approach to the Sun at 0.256 AU (inside Mercury's orbit), moving at ~87.7 km/s at perihelion — far too fast for the Sun to retain it. Nothing on Earth saw it: perihelion occurred ~40 days before discovery, so the entire inbound leg and the solar flyby were unobserved. This gap later mattered enormously — every acceleration measurement and every thermal model had to extrapolate back through a perihelion no one witnessed.

events.title: Closest approach to Earth at ~0.162 AU (still undetected)
events.description: The object passed ~0.16175 AU (~24.2 million km, about 63 lunar distances) from Earth — its minimum Earth distance — five days before anyone found it. It was detected only on the outbound leg, already receding, which compressed the entire global observing campaign into a few frantic weeks before it faded beyond reach of ground-based telescopes.

events.title: Discovery by Robert Weryk / Pan-STARRS1
events.description: Robert Weryk found the fast-moving ~20th-magnitude object (it had peaked at magnitude 19.7 the night before) in Pan-STARRS1 survey images from Haleakala, Hawaii, while searching for near-Earth asteroids. Follow-up astrometry (including pre-discovery images from Oct 18) quickly showed an eccentricity of ~1.2 — the first solidly hyperbolic small body ever recorded, meaning it came from outside the Solar System. Initially designated comet C/2017 U1 (PANSTARRS).

events.title: Designation saga ends: first-ever 'I' class — 1I/'Oumuamua
events.description: A two-week identity crisis: designated comet C/2017 U1 at discovery, reclassified asteroid A/2017 U1 on Oct 25 when deep imaging showed no coma or tail, then on Nov 6 the Minor Planet Center (MPEC 2017-V17) created an entirely new designation class — 'I' for interstellar — making it 1I/'Oumuamua, with the IAU-approved Hawaiian name meaning roughly 'a messenger from afar arriving first' (suggested by the Pan-STARRS team). No object had ever forced the IAU to invent a new category before.

events.title: VLT/Gemini lightcurve: extreme 10:1 elongation (Meech et al., Nature)
events.description: Meech et al. published the coordinated ESO VLT / Gemini / CFHT / UKIRT / Keck lightcurve campaign in Nature: brightness varied by a factor of ~10 every 7.3 hours, implying an axis ratio of at least ~10:1 (later refined to ~6:1–8:1) — more elongated than any known Solar System asteroid or comet. Reddish surface, no dust, no coma, tumbling rotation. The 'cigar' (or 'pancake', per later modeling) shape became anomaly #1 in the alien-tech debate.

events.title: Breakthrough Listen scans 'Oumuamua with Green Bank — radio silence
events.description: Breakthrough Listen pointed the 100-m Green Bank Telescope at 'Oumuamua for the first of four observing blocks (3:45–9:45 pm ET), sweeping 1–12 GHz across the L, S, C and X bands and accumulating 90 TB of raw data over the ~2-hour on-target observation. Sensitivity was good enough to detect a transmitter with the power of a cellphone at the object's distance in under a minute. No artificial signals were found then or in the completed analysis (Enriquez et al. 2018) — the natural-vs-artificial question would instead be fought over dynamics, not radio.

events.title: Non-gravitational acceleration detected (Micheli et al., Nature)
events.description: Micheli et al. reported in Nature that 'Oumuamua's trajectory — reconstructed from ground data plus late Hubble astrometry through January 2018 — required a non-gravitational acceleration of ~4.9e-6 m/s^2 at 1 AU, falling off roughly as 1/r^2. For a comet this is normal outgassing; for an object with no detected coma, dust, or tail it was a paradox. This single measurement is the load-bearing anomaly behind every exotic hypothesis that followed, from hydrogen icebergs to lightsails.

events.title: Bialy & Loeb lightsail paper ignites global media storm
events.description: Shmuel Bialy and Avi Loeb (Harvard CfA) posted 'Could Solar Radiation Pressure Explain 'Oumuamua's Peculiar Acceleration?' (arXiv:1810.11490, published ApJL 868 L1 on 2018-11-12). They showed radiation pressure could produce the observed acceleration if the object were a thin sheet with mass-to-area ratio ~0.1 g/cm^2 — about 0.3–0.9 mm thick, a lightsail geometry — and floated that it 'may be a fully operational probe sent intentionally to Earth vicinity by an alien civilization.' The paper triggered a worldwide media storm and made Loeb the public face of the alien-artifact hypothesis.

events.title: Spitzer non-detection caps the size and rules out normal outgassing
events.description: Trilling et al. (AJ; NASA release Nov 14, 2018) reported that Spitzer stared at 'Oumuamua's position for 30.2 hours on 2017 Nov 21–22 and saw nothing in the infrared. The non-detection capped the size (effective radius roughly 49–220 m depending on albedo, implying a possibly highly reflective surface) and set tight limits on CO/CO2 outgassing — deepening the acceleration paradox: whatever pushed it was not detectable as gas or dust. Bialy & Loeb leaned on these limits.

events.title: ISSI team verdict: 'no compelling evidence to favor an alien explanation' (Nature Astronomy)
events.description: The 14-member International Space Science Institute (ISSI) 'Oumuamua team ('The natural history of 'Oumuamua', Bannister et al., Nature Astronomy) published the mainstream consensus review: every observed property — shape, tumbling, color, acceleration — lies within plausible ranges for a natural interstellar planetesimal, and 'we find no compelling evidence to favor an alien explanation.' Loeb publicly rejected the conclusion; the paper remains the standard natural-origin reference against which his claims are measured.

events.title: Seligman & Laughlin hydrogen-iceberg hypothesis (ApJL)
events.description: Darryl Seligman and Gregory Laughlin proposed (ApJL 896 L8; arXiv:2005.12932) that 'Oumuamua was a hydrogen iceberg formed in the coldest cores of giant molecular clouds: H2 outgassing is nearly invisible (no dust, no detectable coma) yet provides the acceleration, and H2 sublimation sculpting naturally explains the extreme elongation. Critics (including Loeb, and Hoang & Loeb 2020) countered that H2 ice could not survive the interstellar journey — but the paper opened the 'exotic ice' family of natural explanations.

events.title: Loeb publishes 'Extraterrestrial' — the case goes mainstream
events.description: Avi Loeb's book 'Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth' (Houghton Mifflin Harcourt) hit shelves and became an international bestseller, arguing 'Oumuamua's anomalies — the acceleration without a coma, the extreme shape, the unusual initial rest-frame trajectory — are best explained as artificial technology, possibly a defunct lightsail. The book transformed a technical dispute into a public referendum on scientific open-mindedness and directly seeded Loeb's Galileo Project (announced July 2021).

events.title: Desch & Jackson: nitrogen-ice fragment of an exo-Pluto (JGR Planets)
events.description: Steven Desch and Alan Jackson (ASU) published paired papers in JGR: Planets (AGU release Mar 16, 2021) proposing 'Oumuamua was a chip of solid nitrogen ice blasted off a Pluto-like exoplanet ~half a billion years ago: N2 sublimation matches the acceleration with no visible coma, and the high albedo of N2 ice allows a smaller body. Loeb and collaborators (Siraj & Loeb) rebutted that the required mass of exo-Pluto ejecta strains the galactic budget; Desch defended the numbers. The 'nitrogen iceberg' remains a leading natural candidate.

events.title: Bergner & Seligman 'dark comet' H2 answer in Nature — and Loeb's rebuttal
events.description: Jennifer Bergner (Berkeley) and Darryl Seligman published in Nature that cosmic-ray radiolysis of ordinary water ice during 'Oumuamua's interstellar transit created trapped molecular hydrogen; solar warming then released the H2, producing the acceleration with no visible coma — no exotic composition needed. Widely reported as 'mystery solved.' Within days Thiem Hoang and Avi Loeb posted a rebuttal (arXiv:2303.13861; Loeb's Medium essay ''Oumuamua Was Not a Hydrogen-Water Iceberg', Mar 2023) arguing that evaporative cooling by the escaping H2 leaves the surface a factor of ~9 colder than Bergner & Seligman assumed, cutting the H2 thrust below what is required; Bergner countered that the cooling effects do not change the conclusion. The dispute remains unresolved in print.

events.title: Loeb Scale retroactively ranks 'Oumuamua Level 4 (vs Borisov Level 0)
events.description: Amid the 3I/ATLAS debate, Loeb formalized 'The Loeb Scale: Astronomical Classification of Interstellar Objects' (arXiv:2508.09167, submitted Aug 6, 2025; later published in the International Journal of Astrobiology) — a 0-10 anomaly scale for interstellar objects modeled on the Torino Scale (Levels 0-3 natural, 4-7 increasingly anomalous, 8-10 confirmed artificial). Applied retroactively: 1I/'Oumuamua scores Level 4 (multiple unexplained anomalies), 2I/Borisov Level 0 (the perfectly natural control comet), and 3I/ATLAS Level 4. The scale is Loeb's institutionalization of his 1I-vs-2I framing: Borisov is what a normal interstellar comet looks like; 'Oumuamua is not that.

events.title: Outbound: 53.6 AU from the Sun, headed for Pegasus
events.description: Per JPL Horizons, 'Oumuamua is 53.58 AU from the Sun as of today (2026-07-24) — beyond Pluto's average orbit, receding at ~27.0 km/s and asymptotically slowing toward its hyperbolic excess speed of 26.33 km/s, headed for the constellation Pegasus. It passed Neptune's orbital distance in 2022 and is far beyond recovery by any existing telescope; its true nature is now permanently unmeasurable unless a chase mission (e.g. a Project Lyra concept) is ever launched. Every remaining argument is fought over the 2017-2018 data alone.
sources: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/ (COMMAND='1I', heliocentric r on 2026-07-24 = 53.580 AU, range-rate 27.0 km/s)

events.title: Discovery by Gennadiy Borisov at MARGO, Crimea
events.description: Amateur astronomer Gennadiy Borisov discovers a ~magnitude 17.8 comet at low solar elongation using his self-built 0.65 m telescope at his MARGO observatory (MPC code L51) in Nauchnij, Crimea — the first interstellar object ever found by an amateur, and found while it was still inbound (~3 AU from the Sun), unlike 'Oumuamua which was found outbound. It showed a condensed coma and short tail from the start: an unambiguously active comet.

events.title: Provisional designation C/2019 Q4 (Borisov); hyperbolic orbit suspected
events.description: The Minor Planet Center announces the object as comet C/2019 Q4 (Borisov) (MPEC 2019-R106), noting the orbit solution 'has converged to the hyperbolic elements shown below, which would indicate an interstellar origin.' The first published solution gave eccentricity e = 3.08 — far beyond any bound solar-system orbit (later refined to e = 3.36) — with JPL's Farnocchia, Bill Gray, and Dave Tholen independently reaching the same conclusion: a likely interstellar comet flagged within two weeks of discovery.

events.title: First gas detected: cyanogen (CN) with the William Herschel Telescope
events.description: Fitzsimmons et al. detect the CN (0-0) emission band at 388 nm using the 4.2 m William Herschel Telescope + ISIS spectrograph on La Palma (2019 Sep 20.2 UT) — the first spectroscopic detection of gas from any interstellar object. CN production rate (3.7 +/- 0.4) x 10^24 molecules/s at r = 2.7 AU; follow-up work showed 2I is depleted in C2, but overall its gas chemistry looked like a normal solar-system comet (ApJL 885, L9; arXiv:1909.12144).

events.title: Confirmed interstellar: named 2I/Borisov (MPEC 2019-S72)
events.description: The IAU/Minor Planet Center issues MPEC 2019-S72, confirming the interstellar hyperbolic orbit (e = 3.372 in the circular's solution, from 472 observations spanning Aug 30 - Sep 24) and assigning the permanent designation 2I/Borisov — the second interstellar object and the first unambiguous interstellar comet. The IAU retained the discoverer's name, honoring the amateur discovery.

events.title: First Hubble imaging: tiny nucleus, radius under 0.5 km
events.description: HST/WFC3 obtains the sharpest images yet (Jewitt, Luu et al.), beginning a monitoring campaign through perihelion. Convolution modeling of the coma profile sets a nucleus radius limit of r <= 0.5 km (with r > 0.2 km from the non-gravitational acceleration constraint) — roughly 15x smaller than early ground-based estimates (0.7-3.3 km), per NASA's release. A small, ordinary comet nucleus wrapped in dust (Jewitt et al. 2020, ApJL 888, L23; arXiv:1912.05422).

events.title: Perihelion at 2.006 AU
events.description: 2I/Borisov reaches perihelion at 2.006 AU (just outside Mars' orbit), moving ~44 km/s — well above the ~30 km/s local solar escape speed, with a hyperbolic excess velocity of ~32 km/s that guarantees it will leave the solar system. Throughout, it behaves as a classic active comet — sustained water and CO outgassing, dust coma and tail — the natural 'control case' against 'Oumuamua's inert, accelerating anomaly. Hubble imaged it near perihelion on Dec 9.

events.title: Closest approach to Earth: ~1.9 AU
events.description: The comet makes its closest approach to Earth at roughly 1.9 AU (~290 million km) — never a threat and never close, but well-placed for the VLT, ALMA, and Hubble campaigns that bracketed this date: ALMA had observed Dec 15-16, and Bagnulo's VLT/FORS2 polarimetric monitoring spanned late December 2019 through March 2020.

events.title: Double outburst: two brightenings in five days
events.description: Between March 4-9, 2020 (outbound, ~2.8 AU), Polish astronomers Drahus and Guzik (Jagiellonian University) with the OGLE team report the comet brightening ~0.7 magnitudes in two distinct outbursts within days — ~0.3 mag between Mar 4.3-5.3 and ~0.4 mag between Mar 8.3-9.3 UT (ATel #13549, issued Mar 12). Jewitt et al. later measured the ejected dust: ~100 km^2 cross-section, ~2 x 10^7 kg — a warning sign of nucleus instability after perihelion heating.

events.title: Hubble catches the nucleus splitting: transient double nucleus
events.description: HST/WFC3 images from two programs (PI Jewitt, ATel #13611; PI Bolin, ATel #13613, announced early April 2020) reveal a fragment ~0.3 arcsec from the optocenter. A transient 'double nucleus' with ~0.6 km^2 cross-section (~10^5 kg of dust) appears on March 30 — absent March 28 and gone by April 3. Jewitt, Kim & Mutchler interpret it as rotational bursting of meter-sized boulders ejected in the March outburst, not catastrophic disruption: the comet shed a splinter but survived (ApJL 896, L39).

events.title: ALMA: unusually CO-rich coma (Cordiner et al., Nature Astronomy)
events.description: Cordiner, Milam et al. publish ALMA observations (taken 2019 Dec 15-16) detecting HCN and CO — the first direct measurement of gas from another planetary system. CO is 9-26x more abundant relative to water than in average solar-system comets, suggesting 2I/Borisov formed in an extremely cold, CO-ice-rich outer region of its home system, perhaps around a carbon-rich or M-dwarf star (Nature Astronomy 4, 861; the chemically distinct fingerprint of an alien comet).

events.title: VLT polarimetry: 'the most pristine comet ever observed' (Bagnulo et al.)
events.description: Bagnulo et al. publish VLT/FORS2 polarimetry (taken Dec 2019 - Mar 2020) in Nature Communications: 2I/Borisov's polarization exceeds that of all typical comets and its coma is polarimetrically homogeneous, resembling only the unique comet Hale-Bopp. Conclusion: it likely never passed close to any star before ours — possibly the first truly pristine comet ever observed, carrying unaltered material from its birth cloud (Nat. Commun. 12, 1797).

events.title: Atomic nickel vapor in a cold coma (Guzik & Drahus, Nature)
events.description: Guzik & Drahus report gaseous atomic nickel in 2I/Borisov's coma at 2.322 AU (~180 K equilibrium temperature), produced at 0.9 +/- 0.3 x 10^22 atoms/s, likely from photolysis of a short-lived nickel-bearing molecule (Nature 593, 375). Heavy-metal vapor had previously been seen only in ultrahot environments like sungrazing comets. Published back-to-back with Manfroid et al.'s discovery of Fe and Ni vapor in ~20 solar-system comets — a shared, previously unnoticed chemistry linking 2I to home-grown comets and reinforcing its natural-comet status.

events.title: Loeb Scale ranks 2I/Borisov Level 0: the natural control case
events.description: In the wake of 3I/ATLAS, the Interstellar Object Significance Scale ('Loeb Scale') paper by Omer Eldadi, Gershon Tenenbaum, and Avi Loeb (arXiv:2508.09167, submitted Aug 6, 2025; later Int. J. Astrobiology) retroactively scores the three known interstellar objects on its 0-10 scale: 1I/'Oumuamua Level 4 (anomalous), 3I/ATLAS Level 4, and 2I/Borisov Level 0 — fully consistent with natural cometary behavior. Loeb has consistently treated Borisov as the benchmark 'ordinary comet' proving the detection pipeline works, sharpening the contrast with 'Oumuamua's anomalies.

events.title: Outbound: receding toward interstellar space
events.description: 2I/Borisov is far beyond observability, now tens of AU from the Sun and departing on its hyperbolic trajectory at ~32 km/s excess velocity, never to return. Its legacy: it confirmed that other planetary systems make comets much like ours (CN, HCN, dust, outbursts, nickel vapor), yet with distinct fingerprints (extreme CO enrichment, C2 depletion, unusually pristine dust) — the well-behaved sibling that makes 'Oumuamua's and 3I/ATLAS's oddities stand out.

quotes.text: Considering an artificial origin, one possibility is that 'Oumuamua is a lightsail, floating in interstellar space as a debris from an advanced technological equipment.
quotes.speaker: Shmuel Bialy & Abraham Loeb
quotes.source: Bialy & Loeb, 'Could Solar Radiation Pressure Explain 'Oumuamua's Peculiar Acceleration?', ApJL 868 L1 (arXiv:1810.11490, posted 2018-10-26)
quotes.context: The lightsail sentence from the paper that launched the alien-technology hypothesis; verified verbatim against the arXiv full text.
quotes.verify_note: dropped the article in the source's own phrasing: the paper reads 'as a debris from an advanced technological equipment'

quotes.text: Alternatively, a more exotic scenario is that 'Oumuamua may be a fully operational probe sent intentionally to Earth vicinity by an alien civilization.
quotes.speaker: Shmuel Bialy & Abraham Loeb
quotes.context: The paper's most-quoted line, immediately following the lightsail-debris suggestion; verified verbatim against the arXiv full text.

quotes.text: 'Oumuamua was like a buoy resting in the expanse of the universe, and our solar system was like a ship that ran into it at high speed.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.source: Loeb, 'Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth' (Houghton Mifflin Harcourt)
quotes.context: Loeb's signature buoy analogy from his bestselling book — 'Oumuamua as a stationary object the solar system ran into, echoing its LSR-rest-frame kinematics.

quotes.text: If radiation pressure is the accelerating force, then 'Oumuamua represents a new class of thin interstellar material, either produced naturally . . . or is of an artificial origin.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Loeb's book-form framing of the radiation-pressure argument; near-identical sentence appears in the 2018 paper. Verified via published book excerpts.

quotes.text: Thus, we find no compelling evidence to favor an alien explanation for 'Oumuamua.
quotes.speaker: The 'Oumuamua ISSI Team (Bannister, Meech, Knight, Fitzsimmons et al.)
quotes.context: The 14-expert International Space Science Institute team's formal verdict, closing the section that assessed the artificial hypothesis; verified verbatim from the paper PDF.

quotes.text: Assertions that 'Oumuamua may be artificial are not justified when the wide body of current knowledge about solar system minor bodies and planetary formation is considered.
quotes.speaker: The 'Oumuamua ISSI Team
quotes.source: 'The Natural History of 'Oumuamua', Nature Astronomy — Conclusions section
quotes.context: The paper's concluding rebuttal sentence; verified verbatim from the arXiv PDF Conclusions.

quotes.text: We have never seen anything like 'Oumuamua in our solar system. It's really a mystery still.
quotes.speaker: Matthew Knight
quotes.source: University of Maryland press release for the ISSI Nature Astronomy paper
quotes.context: ISSI team co-lead acknowledging the object remains strange even while ruling it natural — the honest tension in the official position.

quotes.text: The alien spacecraft hypothesis is a fun idea, but our analysis suggests there is a whole host of natural phenomena that could explain it.
quotes.speaker: Matthew Knight
quotes.source: University of Maryland / ISSI team press release (also carried by Sci-News, EurekAlert)
quotes.context: The ISSI team's public-facing dismissal of the Loeb lightsail interpretation.

quotes.text: This unusually large variation in brightness means that the object is highly elongated: about ten times as long as it is wide, with a complex, convoluted shape.
quotes.speaker: Karen Meech
quotes.source: ESO press release eso1737, 'ESO Observations Show First Interstellar Asteroid is Like Nothing Seen Before' (VLT results, Meech et al. Nature 552)
quotes.context: Discovery-team lead describing the record 10:1 elongation from the VLT lightcurve; she added it was 'completely inert, without the faintest hint of dust around it.'

quotes.text: I think it's a remnant from another solar system. It's just something that happened to run into us, and we were very lucky to have been operating the telescope that night and looking in that direction.
quotes.speaker: Robert Weryk
quotes.source: CBC News interview, 'Oumuamua not an alien probe, says scientist who discovered it' (also carried by Fox News 2018-11-12)
quotes.context: The Pan-STARRS astronomer who discovered 'Oumuamua, dismissing the Bialy-Loeb lightsail idea as 'wild speculation' — 'we actually believe that's not true based on the data we obtained.'
quotes.verify_note: sentence was truncated five words early and closed with a period; restored in full. Interview date corrected 2018-11-06 -> 2018-11-12 (CBC publication date)

quotes.text: I saw a moving object in the frame, it moved in a direction that was slightly different from that of main asteroids.
quotes.speaker: Gennadiy Borisov
quotes.source: RIA Novosti interview (translated from Russian; as cited on the 2I/Borisov Wikipedia discovery account)
quotes.context: The Crimean amateur astronomer describing the 2019-08-30 pre-dawn discovery of 2I/Borisov with his self-built 0.65 m telescope at MARGO observatory. English is a translation.

quotes.text: Every amateur … dreams of discovering something unusual and extraordinary. When you manage to do that, you feel joy and happiness, and you set a new task.
quotes.speaker: Gennadiy Borisov
quotes.source: Space.com Q&A with Meghan Bartels (email interview via Roscosmos), published on 2I/Borisov's perihelion day
quotes.context: Borisov on what the discovery meant to him, published the day his comet reached perihelion (~2 AU).

quotes.text: 2I/Borisov could represent the first truly pristine comet ever observed.
quotes.speaker: Stefano Bagnulo
quotes.source: ESO press release eso2106, 'First interstellar comet may be the most pristine ever found' (VLT polarimetry; Bagnulo et al., Nature Communications)
quotes.context: The 'most pristine comet' line: VLT polarimetry showed 2I/Borisov more pristine than Hale-Bopp, apparently never having passed close to any star — the classic-comet control case to 'Oumuamua.

quotes.text: 1I/'Oumuamua is anomalous relative to 2I/Borisov and 3I/ATLAS … it had an extreme disk-like shape, it exhibited a non-gravitational acceleration and it did not show any evidence for cometary activity.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.source: Loeb, 'Origin and Age of Three Interstellar Objects: 1I/'Oumuamua, 2I/Borisov, and 3I/ATLAS', Medium essay
quotes.context: Loeb's retrospective three-object comparison after 3I/ATLAS's discovery: Borisov and ATLAS behave like comets, 'Oumuamua still stands apart. Ellipsis trims 'not only because it is much younger than they are.' Verified verbatim.

quotes.text: 3I/ATLAS is most likely a comet of natural origin, but there are 8 anomalies that endow it with a rank of 4 on the Loeb scale.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.source: Loeb, 'Updating the Loeb Classification Scale of 3I/ATLAS', Medium (the Loeb scale itself defined in Trivedi & Loeb, arXiv:2508.09167, Aug 2025)
quotes.context: Loeb applying his 0-10 anomaly scale to 3I/ATLAS; the companion Loeb-scale framework retroactively treats 2I/Borisov as a rank-0 natural baseline while 'Oumuamua keeps an elevated rank. Verified verbatim from the Medium essay.
